title: consolidated-token-orchestration-for-rotations-expiry-and-scope-visibility
creator: Nina Valdez
description:
Problem: Our current token surface is inconsistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments: naming conventions vary, rotation is ad-hoc (cron jobs in multiple services), expiry semantics differ (hard-expiry vs soft-grace windows), and audit trails are fragmented. This makes incident response slow, introduces rollback risk for canary rollouts, and complicates least-privilege enforcement for per-scope keys.

Goal: Build a single 'Token Orchestration' service and admin surface that: consolidates rotation scheduling, enforces standard naming and provenance metadata, implements configurable soft-expiry windows with automated revocation, exposes scope-aware search and ownership in Console, and emits unified audit events compatible with our logging pipeline and SIEM. The service must support Hosted API tokens, Dedicated service keys, and Private deployment tokens (including on-prem KMS integrations).

Scope: 
- Rotation scheduler and coordinator (central queue + per-customer rate limits)
- Naming policy enforcement and automated tagging (env, scope, owner, created_by)
- Per-scope key issuance and contract for least-privilege scoping
- Soft-expiry semantics: pre-expiry notifications, grace window, automated revoke and post-revocation audit events
- Token provenance tracking for incident triage (who issued, last rotated, linked PRs or ACL changes)
- Console UI additions: token ledger view, filters by scope/owner/age, rotation controls
- Audit logging: standardized event schema, required fields, and retention notes for compliance teams

Non-goals: Re-implement RBAC v2; this ticket will integrate with the RBAC v2 system but not design role model. Full token migration automation for all customers will be follow-up work.
acceptance_criteria: Token Orchestration service deployed to staging and can schedule rotations for test tokens without divergence across deployments
Naming policy enforced on new token creation; existing tokens flagged for migration with automated tagging
Soft-expiry workflow implemented: notification -> grace window -> revoke; verified by end-to-end test
Audit events emitted to the centralized logging pipeline with required schema fields (token_id, actor, action, previous_state, new_state, reason)
Console shows token ledger with filters for scope/owner/created_by and supports manual rotation command with audit trail
Documentation (PRD + runbook) linked and security review completed
comments: 2026-02-16 Nina Valdez: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed on central queue approach to avoid per-service cron drift. Action: Marcus to prototype coordinator with Redis stream for ordering.

2026-02-22 Marcus Lee: Prototype complete in feature/token-orch-coordinator branch. Observed race when multiple rotations for same customer scheduled simultaneously; added per-customer lock and exponential backoff.

2026-02-27 Security review (initial): Julia Park - requested explicit retention policy for token metadata in audit logs and clarified fields required for compliance exports (added to acceptance criteria).

2026-03-03 Design feedback: Priya Menon - Console token ledger UX: add quick filters for 'expiring in 7 days' and 'scoped to project' and show last rotated timestamp. Marcus to add API endpoints for these filters.

2026-03-06 Engineering note: Chose soft-expiry pattern (notify -> grace -> revoke) over immediate hard-expiry to reduce customer disruption; trade-off: slightly longer window after compromise but much lower support noise. Logging will mark tokens 'pending_revocation' during grace window.

2026-03-10 QA update: End-to-end test for rotation workflow flaky when connected to on-prem KMS; root cause: network timeout threshold too low. Increasing KMS timeouts and adding retry fence fixed tests.
2026-03-12 Nina Valdez: Security review completed; PRD updated with required SIEM mapping. Preparing for staged rollout to 10% of customers next week.
implementation_notes: Coordinator will be implemented as a new service under platform/team/security with a Redis stream-backed queue and per-owner locks to serialize rotations
Naming policy: prefix <team|customer>-<scope>-<env>-<shorthash> and tags for user:owner_id, issue_ref(optional), created_by
Soft-expiry: default notify at 7 days before expiry, grace window 72 hours (configurable per-customer), configurable auto-revoke after grace
Audit schema: use event_type token.rotation, token.revoke, token.create with standardized fields agreed with SIEM team
Migration plan: run scanner to flag tokens that violate naming or lack scope; produce migration tickets and notify owners via Console and email
Console changes: new token ledger route /api/v1/admin/tokens with filter params; UI to call existing admin audit endpoints for history
